notes: Answer as one set covering 56 places: the 50 states, D.C., Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands, plus federal taxes.
Rules only, never observations. Mark anything not found as UNKNOWN rather than borrowing another place's rule.

title: Where each state and territory stands today on each policy question the game asks
question: For each of the 56 places and each policy question in the game's state-and-local catalog (127 issues, docs and src/simulation/policy-pack-us-state-and-local.ts) and federal catalog (src/simulation/policy-pack-us-federal.ts): what the law currently in force answers, yes, no, or partly, with the statute or constitutional provision and its effective date. Where a question is decided locally, say whether the state leaves it to local governments, preempts it, or has no rule. Mark anything not found as UNKNOWN; do not fill a gap from another place.
usableAnswer: One row per place per question: current answer (yes, no, partly with what part), the provision and effective date, whether it is preempted or left local, and an evidence status.
whyItMatters: A passed bill will now record where its state stands on the question it answers, so the next bill, the members and the voters can read the law in force. A game opens with no such record, so every place starts as UNKNOWN until this answer seeds it; without it the first bill on any question would pretend nothing was law before it.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: A measure lists which questions it is about; nothing records which way any law in force answers them.
